summary.text: A 62-year-old woman, widowed and working as a seamstress, with hypertension, autoimmune thyroiditis with hypothyroidism, an anxiety disorder and congenital right-sided sensorineural hearing loss was referred to an autoimmune disease clinic for left-sided fluctuating sensorineural hearing loss that began two years earlier and responded to corticosteroids. Bell’s palsy one year before consultation resolved with corticosteroids.

While awaiting assessment she developed recurrent low-grade fevers, upper respiratory infections and otitis media with tympanic membrane perforation. At the first visit she reported no active autoimmune symptoms and the examination was unremarkable. One month later she developed nonpruritic, erythematous, scaly skin lesions and new cervical and submandibular lymphadenopathy, and psoriasis guttata was suspected.

HIV testing returned positive with a high viral load of 128,000 copies/mL, and she was referred urgently to infectious disease and started on dolutegravir/lamivudine. PET-CT showed extensive hypermetabolic lymphadenopathy and active aortic vasculitis; the lymph node biopsy showed reactive changes without evidence of malignancy or infection.

Early in ART she developed oral candidosis and vulvar condylomas, and screening for opportunistic infections was negative. She no longer had skin lesions at the dermatology consultation, so no biopsy was done, and she had no recurrence of psoriasis lesions or hearing loss since starting ART. She is responding well and is due for reevaluation in April 2026.
